title: Iff split for the comparison-encoding lemma gtFelt_eq_one_iff
intent: Characterise the field-element encoding `gtFelt` by proving `gtFelt a b = 1 ↔ a.val > b.val`, splitting the iff with `constructor` so that each direction is discharged by a dedicated one-line lemma that unfolds the definitional `if`.

parent.name: gtFelt_eq_one_iff
parent.statement: theorem gtFelt_eq_one_iff (a b : Felt) : gtFelt a b = 1 ↔ a.val > b.val := by

children.name: gtFelt_of_gt
children.statement: theorem gtFelt_of_gt (a b : Felt) (h : a.val > b.val) : gtFelt a b = 1 := by

children.name: gtFelt_of_not_gt
children.statement: theorem gtFelt_of_not_gt (a b : Felt) (h : ¬ a.val > b.val) : gtFelt a b = 0 := by

applicability.goal_shape: an iff (or antisymmetry) between a definitional encoding taking a fixed value and the decidable condition the encoding represents: here (gtFelt a b = 1) ↔ (a.val > b.val), where gtFelt a b is `if a.val > b.val then 1 else 0`
applicability.use_when: each direction can be stated as its own lemma whose proof is a single simp/unfold over the definition, and the two values the encoding takes (1 and 0) are distinct constants so the contradictory branch closes by norm_num
applicability.avoid_when: the forward direction needs a real argument rather than a one-line unfold-and-contradiction; the encoding is not already simp-normal form; the condition is not decidable; or the two directions need unrelated proofs

claims.claim: The parent proof closes each direction with exactly one of the two children: `constructor` (line 39) yields two goals, the forward one rewrites with `gtFelt_of_not_gt a b hab` at h (line 42) and the backward one applies `gtFelt_of_gt a b h` (line 45).
Each child is closed by `simp [gtFelt, h]` alone (lines 27 and 30), with no other lemma or tactic in either proof.
Shape: the main theorem's glue is 8 lines (38-45), assembled from 2 direct lemmas whose proofs are 1 line each, so the longest project-lemma chain below the theorem has depth 1.
claims.evidence: read of the whole copied file code/plugins/writing-lean-proofs/evals/cases/03-normal-form/input/WordCmp.lean; parent = L38-L45, child proofs = L27 and L30, direct_lemmas = 2

claims.claim: The parent is reused as a leaf: `ltFelt_eq_one_iff` reduces to it in one line, `simp only [ltFelt, gtFelt_eq_one_iff]` (line 48).
The file's module docstring states the purpose these lemmas serve: "Field-element encodings of comparisons on canonical representatives, used to model the VM's `gt`/`lt` instructions."

metrics.how_counted: parent = lines 38-45 of the copied file (theorem statement plus by-block); child proofs = the single simp line of each child, line 27 (gtFelt_of_gt) and line 30 (gtFelt_of_not_gt)

consequences: constructor on the iff creates two goals, one per direction. The forward direction is the only one with real work: it must exclude the case gtFelt a b = 0 by contradiction (by_contra, rewrite with gtFelt_of_not_gt, then absurd 1 = 0 via norm_num). The backward direction is a direct application of gtFelt_of_gt. Failure modes: the contradiction step relies on the encoding's two values (1 and 0) being distinct and norm_num knowing 0 ≠ 1; if the encoding took the same value on both branches, or if the negation branch were not a single simp, the forward direction would need its own lemma.
